- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., -0.43 to -0.70 in sentiment history).
- Underestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.37 or +0.30) — model tends to lag or overcorrect.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often overshoots mid- to late horizon (e.g., 82+ in 30d forecast) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70), model tends to overreact with sharp upward moves — correct by reducing forecast slope.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–3) when sentiment is mixed — use smoother transition from recent history.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust downward — correct by slightly lowering forecast mid-horizon.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast often overcorrect — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
